issues.legal_issue: A land acquisition is invalid when the acquisition power is used to pursue an extraneous private end rather than the statutory public purpose.
material_facts: The land was selected for acquisition for a grain market, but the landowners alleged that the selection was driven by a politically influential person’s private hostility toward them.
An earlier acquisition of the same land had been quashed on mala fides, and the State later initiated a fresh acquisition of that land.
The record supported the conclusion that the stated public purpose was used as a pretext to deprive the landowners of their property for a private end.
issues.conclusion: The acquisition was vitiated by mala fides and could not be sustained because the power was used for an end beyond its statutory purpose.
issues.legal_principle: The Land Acquisition Act, 1894, including Sections 4 and 6, entrusts land selection to the Government’s discretion, subject to constitutional limits including Articles 14, 19 and 31 as then applicable. A court does not substitute its view for the executive’s choice of land merely because the choice appears unwise, but may intervene when power is polluted by an oblique end. Fraud on power or colourable exercise occurs when an official power is used, under the appearance of pursuing its lawful purpose, to attain an end outside the purpose for which it was entrusted; it invalidates the action whether the extraneous end is malicious or otherwise. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The government undertook a proceeding to acquire privately owned land.
predicates.power_used_for_extraneous_private_end: The acquisition power was used to pursue a private end unrelated to the authorized public purpose.

issues.definition: When a land acquisition proceeding uses the acquisition power to pursue an extraneous private end, the acquisition is invalid.

issues.legal_issue: Emergency acquisition powers may not be used to dispense with a hearing unless genuine urgency makes even the minimum time for a hearing incompatible with the public interest.
material_facts: The acquisition process had remained inactive for years before the State revived it and invoked emergency powers to take the land.
The State used the emergency procedure to dispense with the statutory inquiry that would otherwise allow the affected landowners to be heard.
The circumstances did not establish an urgency that could not brook the minimum time needed for a hearing.
issues.conclusion: The resort to emergency powers to dispense with the inquiry was unjustified; a long-dormant process suddenly treated as urgent was a travesty of emergency power.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 17 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, read with the hearing protection associated with Section 5A and the requirements of Articles 14 and 19, the inquiry should not be dispensed with except in real urgency where public interest cannot tolerate even the minimum time required to hear affected owners. Compulsory taking of property is serious, and hearing the owner helps prevent arbitrary action. No earlier cases are cited for this principle in the judgment.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The government undertook a proceeding to acquire privately owned land.
predicates.emergency_shortcut_used: The government invoked an emergency procedure to take land without the ordinary opportunity for a hearing.
predicates.no_genuine_immediate_urgency: The circumstances did not require taking the land so immediately that even the minimum time for a hearing could not be allowed.

issues.definition: If an emergency shortcut is used in a land acquisition proceeding without genuine immediate urgency, dispensing with the hearing is unjustified.

issues.legal_issue: A finding of mala fides may be upheld where the allegations are supported by the history of the matter and are not denied by a person with direct knowledge, and the finding is not shown to be perverse or unsupported by evidence.
material_facts: The landowners alleged that a politically influential person had pressured the authorities to select their land for private reasons.
That person was given an opportunity to respond to the allegations but did not contradict them.
The State’s affidavit was verified by an official who was not a participant in the land-selection deliberations and relied on official records rather than personal knowledge.
The history included an earlier acquisition of the same land being quashed for mala fides and a later renewed attempt to acquire it.
The Supreme Court found no perversity, absence of evidence, or similar basis for disturbing the High Court’s factual conclusion.
issues.conclusion: The allegations of mala fides were properly accepted, the High Court’s conclusion was not displaced, and the State’s petition for special leave was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: A factual finding is not upset unless it is shown to rest on a perverse assessment, an absence of evidence, or a comparable defect. Where the material allegations concern deliberations known directly only to the decision-makers, an affidavit from a person without direct knowledge does not controvert them; the absence of a denial from a person with personal knowledge, considered with the history of the matter, may support accepting the allegations. The judgment applies this principle in reviewing the High Court’s decision in a special-leave proceeding and cites no earlier cases for it.

rule.if: special_leave_proceeding_against_quashing_of_acquisition and mala_fides_alleged and no_denial_by_person_with_direct_knowledge and record_supports_allegations and no_perversity_or_evidentiary_failure

predicates.special_leave_proceeding_against_quashin: The government sought special leave to challenge a judgment quashing an acquisition.
predicates.mala_fides_alleged: The affected owners alleged that the acquisition power was exercised in bad faith for an extraneous purpose.
predicates.no_denial_by_person_with_direct_knowledg: No person with personal and direct knowledge of the relevant decision-making denied the allegations despite an opportunity to do so.
predicates.record_supports_allegations: The history and other material in the record supported the allegations of bad faith.
predicates.no_perversity_or_evidentiary_failure: The challenging party did not show that the lower court’s factual finding was perverse or unsupported by evidence.

issues.definition: In a special-leave proceeding challenging the quashing of an acquisition, a supported mala fides finding is upheld when it is not denied by a person with direct knowledge and is not shown to be perverse or unsupported.
